name: Accessibility permission requested out of context after app/link delivery
description: A message or app impersonating a trusted service asks the recipient to grant an Android Accessibility permission, which gives the app screen-reading and input-injection control. The signal is the out-of-context Accessibility request combined with a fake-app/link delivery vector.

source_references.document_ref: Advisory TAU-ADV-012 — Android GOD Mode (original PDF unavailable)

manual_retrieval.official_alternate_source: CyberDost / I4C, Ministry of Home Affairs — https://t.me/s/cyberdosti4c/4267
manual_retrieval.notes: Original advisory PDF still unavailable (SRC-019 stays RETRIEVAL_FAILED). The official I4C CyberDost post states Android God Mode abuses Accessibility permissions, impersonates trusted services, and is delivered via links/APKs/fake apps. OFFICIAL_ALTERNATE caps this rule at PARTIAL (ADR-0015).

explanation.plain: An app or link asked you to switch on an Accessibility permission. That permission lets an app read your screen and tap for you — enough to empty your accounts. Do not enable it for an app you were sent through a message.
explanation.technical: ACCESSIBILITY_PERMISSION_REQUEST (device-action) combined with a fake-app/link delivery vector. Matches the I4C CyberDost Android God Mode description.
verification_steps: Never grant Accessibility to an app delivered by a link or message.
Uninstall the app and check Settings > Accessibility for anything you did not deliberately enable.
explanation.why_confidence_limited: Evidence is an official I4C CyberDost channel post (OFFICIAL_ALTERNATE), not the formal advisory PDF. Implementability is PARTIAL: the permission grant itself is a device-side signal, so from text TrustLens sees the request but not the grant. Held at APPROVED, capped at PARTIAL.

provenance.notes: UNSUPPORTED at Phase 1 (SRC-019 unreachable, G-01).
